Learning support that starts with the learner

NOBILVA was an education organization I founded to support children facing barriers to attending school. The work combined an AI learning chatbot with the organization needed to bring that support to students across Japan.

The product served elementary and middle school learners. That shaped how I approached explanations: the responses needed to be appropriate for the student’s age and break the material into manageable steps.

Designing how the chatbot explains

I built the learning chatbot with Python and the OpenAI API. My work included engineering system prompts and response constraints for age-appropriate, step-by-step explanations.

This work focused on the behavior of the learning experience: how the model should respond, how much it should explain at once, and how to make its answers useful for a younger learner. The chatbot supported more than 5,000 interactions.

Building the organization around the product

Alongside development, I led a 17-member team and helped the organization reach more than 150 students. The role connected product development with coordinating people and finding support for the organization.

I secured government funding and promotional support. Those forms of support helped establish a foundation for the organization’s educational work.

Recognition and what I take forward

NOBILVA received the national Grand Prize at the Japan AI Education Utilization Award, placing first among 477 teams.

For me, the project brought software development and team leadership into the same problem: making a technical idea work for the people it is meant to support. I carry that connection into my later work on conversational AI and useful scientific software.
